# S261 — Shared role matrix: apply ork's matrix to one project or to every registered project

*Proposed.* The owner tells ork to copy the role matrix of one registered project (ork's own, as the owner asked) to another registered project, or to every registered project at once, so that the matrices unify. ork reads both matrices with `slicer relay-roles show --json`, builds a whole-matrix change set that keeps each target's own spec check and UI pass rows and the rules that name them, rewrites the row ids that copied rule text names to the target's ids, and writes it through slicer's atomic `relay-roles apply` replace form (S250, slicer s443 and s444) after a dry run the owner confirms per project. The design questions Q1-Q8 are answered (see `Open owner questions`); the command and method names are `ork roles matrix copy` and `matrix.copy` (Q7, owner 2026-11-25).

**Findings:** Owner 2026-11-03: the owner should be able to tell ork to apply its relay roles matrix to any project so the matrices unify, or to all registered projects at once. Facts (read with slicer relay-roles show, 2026-11-03): the matrices differ per project. ork has 20 rows and 3 gpt-6.1-sol rows; slicer 18 and 5; daystar 12 and 2; adjudicate 9, pitfight 8 and squalify 8 have no Codex rows. slicer owns the matrix (.slicer/relay-roles.json, changed only through slicer relay-roles commands); S173 edits one project row by row, S250 applies a change set atomically through a proposed slicer relay-roles apply. Needed first: check that slicer has no such capability or roadmap item, then spec it with owner questions: the source (ork's own project matrix or a stored master), what is copied (rows, rules, or both), project-specific rows to keep (the spec-check row and rule, notes), dry run and per-project confirm, and the apply-to-all mode. ## Why

Owner, 2026-11-03: the owner should be able to tell ork to apply its own relay roles matrix to any registered project, so the project matrices unify, or to all registered projects at once.

Facts read on 2026-11-03:
- The matrices differ per project. `slicer relay-roles show --json --root DIR`: ork has 26 rows after commit f3d34f9 (3 gpt-6.1-sol and 6 gpt-6.1-terra Codex rows, 4 Grok rows with model `latest`) and rules u1, u3-u11; slicer has 18 rows (5 gpt-6.1-sol rows, 3 Grok rows pinned to `grok-4.7`) and rules u1-u10; adjudicate has 9 rows, no Codex row, and keeps rule u2 "No cross-vendor reviewer unless the owner asks", which ork dropped today (f3d34f9). The owner's figures for daystar (12 rows, 2 sol), pitfight (8) and squalify (8) were not re-read here: those repos are outside this workspace.
- Row ids and rule ids differ per project, and the same id means different things: the Spec check row is r16 in ork (rule u11), r18 in slicer (rule u10) and r9 in adjudicate (rule u6); rule u2 bars a cross-vendor reviewer in adjudicate and allows one in slicer.
- Rule text names row ids. ork's u8 names r8, r4, r9, r12, r15 and r3; u10 names r14; u11 names r16 and r14. A row copied to another project gets a new id there, so copied rule text must be rewritten, or it points at the wrong row.
- Some rules are ork-specific: u10 names `internal/tui`, `docs/dashboard.md` and the skills enabled in ork's `.claude/settings.json`; u7 names record 124 and `ork run PARENT --slivers`. Some rows carry project notes (adjudicate r1, r2, r4: "owner 2026-10-15: Haiku replaced after sandbox-rul...").
- ork reads the spec-check and UI-pass rows only through rule text: `SpecCheckRowID` matches `Spec check row \((r\d+)\)` and `UIPassRowID` matches `UI pass row \((r\d+)\)` (`internal/slicercli/write.go:240-266`). `planRun` drops both rows from the reviewer and gate chains (`internal/daemon/runs.go:386-424`), and the spec check refuses a matrix without that rule (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:94-96`). A unified matrix must keep a spec-check row and a rule that names its id in that project.
- ork's `slicercli.Row` has no condition fields (`internal/slicercli/types.go:214-222`), while `show --json` gives each row a `when` object (size, effort, importance, urgency, well_specified, split, sliver). Copying a row needs `when`.
- `matrixAdapters` maps only `claude code` and `codex` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:345-346`, adj 155); Grok rows are skipped by ork's plans but used by relays that ork does not run.

slicer (checked as AGENTS.md asks, `slicer find` in ../slicer on 2026-11-03 for matrix, relay-roles, relay roles, apply, replace, copy, sync, template, global, user-level, default matrix, shared matrix, master):
- No slicer command copies or unifies a matrix across projects, and no item plans one. slicer s443 (`relay-roles-apply`, open, v1.20) names "a user-level (global) default matrix" under Not in this slice.
- slicer s444 (`relay-roles-replace`, open, v1.20, depends on s443) is the write primitive this slice needs: a complete matrix that replaces the current one in one atomic, validated write with `expect` and `--dry-run`; its Why says "A tool can copy a matrix from one project to another". Its rules: a row or rule with an `id` must exist in the target (else `unknown_role_row` or `unknown_role_rule`); one without `id` is added with the next id; absent ids are removed; rules have no move verb, so a replace whose rule order the derived steps cannot reach is refused with `usage`. Its test `test_RelayRolesApply_Replace_FromAnotherProject` covers rows of project A without their ids replaced into B.
- The installed slicer is 1.18.0, which has no `relay-roles apply` (`slicer relay-roles --help` lists show, recommend, init, add, set, remove, move, rule-add, rule-edit, rule-remove).

ork items: S250 (`matrix-apply`, open, v1.2) passes a change set, `ops` or `replace`, to `slicer relay-roles apply` for one project and returns slicer's result with adapter warnings; S173 (`matrix.edit`, open, v1.1) runs one `relay-roles` verb per call; S226 (matrix editor in the TUI, depends on S173) and S251 (project settings pane) are the TUI places. None of them copies a matrix between projects. This slice builds on S250's `RelayRolesApply` client call.

No adj question is filed by this draft; the owner questions are below.

Boundary: slicer owns `.slicer/relay-roles.json` (`docs/boundaries.md:14`); ork builds the change set and passes it to slicer, never edits the file. Each write lands in the target project's main checkout and stays uncommitted (owner, 2026-10-29, S173 note). A run already started keeps its lineup (`runrec.Record.Lineup`); a launch plan that the copy changes is refused by the `plan changed` check at `run.start`.

Wire (*proposed*, assuming the recommended answers): `matrix.copy {from, to?: [names], all?: bool, dry_run?: bool}`. Exactly one of `to` and `all`. `from` is never a target; `all` means every registered project except `from`. Result `{from, projects: [{project, status, steps?, warnings?, error?}], partial}` where `status` is `would change`, `unchanged`, `changed`, `skipped` or `failed`; `error` is slicer's or ork's code and message unchanged; `partial` is true when some projects changed and some failed.

Update (2026-11-25, fix round 1): the bullet that says ork reads the spec-check and UI-pass rows only through rule text is out of date. Since S258 and S344 ork also reads the project's `spec_check_rows` and `ui_pass_rows` settings, and S304's `Local spec check row (rNN)` and `Local UI pass row (rNN)` rules name trial rows (`specCheckRowSet` and `uiPassRowSet`, `internal/daemon/speccheck.go`). Each of them keeps such a row out of the reviewer and gate chains. Owner decision 2026-11-24, `matrix.copy-settings-rows`: the copy keeps by id every row of the target's spec check and UI pass sets (the rows its rules name, the rows its settings list and its Local trial rows) and the rules that name them, and does not copy the same sets of the source.

## Implement

1. Preconditions are met (2026-11-25): the owner has answered Q1-Q8 (see `Open owner questions`), S250 has landed, and the installed slicer (1.22.1) has `relay-roles apply` with `replace`. Check `slicer --version` anyway.
2. Write the failing tests; see each fail for the reason given.
3. `Row.When` in `internal/slicercli/types.go`. Check that `go test ./...` still passes with the new field before going on.
4. Planner (pure), `planMatrixCopy(sourceProject, source, project, target)`: the rows a project keeps are its spec check and UI pass sets, `specCheckRowSet` and `uiPassRowSet` of `internal/daemon/speccheck.go`: the rows its `Spec check row (rNN)` and `UI pass row (rNN)` rules name, the rows of its `spec_check_rows` and `ui_pass_rows` settings, and its `Local spec check row` and `Local UI pass row` trial rows (owner decision 2026-11-24, `matrix.copy-settings-rows`). Build `replace.rows` from the source rows without ids, in source order, except that a source row of the source's own such sets is not copied and the target's kept rows take their places by id (at the end when the source has none). A target row equal to a copied source row is kept by id, so a second copy changes nothing. Build `replace.rules` as the target's rules that name a kept row first, in target order (slicer's replace needs them first), then the source's other rules without ids, in source order; a source rule that names a row of the source's sets is not copied. A target with no `Spec check row (rNN)` rule is refused (`no_spec_check_row`).
5. Handler: resolve `from` and each target with `d.registered`; read both matrices; plan with both registered projects; call `RelayRolesApply` (S250) with `--dry-run`; map each copied source row id to the id the dry run's `add` steps report (they keep the order given; verified on slicer 1.22.1); rewrite rule text; refuse a copied rule that names a row that is not copied. Check every target with a dry run before any write; then write each target with `expect` set to its dry run's `revision_before`, one project at a time, and record each outcome. Writes use a zero `runrec.Writer{}` like `item.note` (`internal/daemon/items.go:34-49`) and land uncommitted.
6. Wire, dispatch, client call.
7. CLI `ork roles matrix copy FROM (TO... | --all) [--dry-run] [--yes] [--json]`: a dry-run call, the preview, a question per project unless `--yes`, then one write call with the confirmed targets.
8. Docs; changelog last (`slicer changelog add`).
9. Do not touch `internal/tui`, `internal/daemon/runs.go` (read `matrixAdapters` only), S173's `matrix.edit`, S250's `matrix.apply` handler, or the matrix of this repository.

Owner decisions (2026-11-25): Where does the unified matrix come from (Q1)? -> named project: `ork roles matrix copy FROM ...`, the owner names the source on each call (no new state) [matrix.copy-source]. What does the copy replace, rows and rules or rows only (Q2)? -> rows and rules: the target is replaced except the parts it keeps (Q3); true unification, but ork-specific rules u7 and u10 and slicer's `grok-4.7` pins land in projects they do not describe [matrix.copy-scope]. What does each target keep of its own (Q3)? -> keep own: each target keeps its spec-check row and rule and its UI-pass row and rule; the source's are not copied; a target with no spec-check rule is refused with `no_spec_check_row`; a copied rule that names a skipped row (ork's u11 names r14) is refused [matrix.copy-keep]. How are the dry run and the confirmation done (Q4)? -> per project: always a dry run first, show slicer's steps and warnings, ask `[y/N]` for each project (Enter is No); `--yes` skips the questions; `--dry-run` stops after the preview [matrix.copy-confirm]. What does apply-to-all do when a project fails (Q5)? -> check all first: dry-run every target and write nothing if any dry run fails; then write each project with `expect`, carry on after a write failure, report each status, `partial: true`, exit 1 [matrix.copy-all]. Where does the copy appear and what is it called (Q7)? -> CLI and daemon: `ork roles matrix copy FROM (TO... | --all)` and the method `matrix.copy`; a TUI action is a later item on S226 or S251 [matrix.copy-surface].

Owner decision (2026-11-24, reported in the fix round): which rows does a target keep (matrix.copy-keep, widened)? -> keep-settings: every row of the target's spec check and UI pass sets, that is the rows its rules name, the rows its `spec_check_rows` and `ui_pass_rows` settings list and its Local trial rows, and the rules that name them; the same sets of the source are not copied [matrix.copy-settings-rows].

## Open owner questions

The questions from the 2026-11-03 spec drafting are answered; they are kept here as the record of what was chosen. Q6 and Q8 were settled by the 2026-11-10 note (v1.2, depends on S250); Q1-Q5 and Q7 were answered by the owner on 2026-11-25 (see the owner decisions under `Implement`).

- Q1 Source of the unified matrix: (a) a project named on each call, `ork roles matrix copy FROM ...` [matrix.copy-source].
- Q2 What is copied, replace or merge: (a) rows and rules, the target replaced except the parts it keeps [matrix.copy-scope].
- Q3 What each target keeps of its own: (a) its spec-check row and rule and its UI-pass row and rule; the source's are not copied; no spec-check rule is refused with `no_spec_check_row`; a copied rule that names a skipped row is refused with `copy_conflict` [matrix.copy-keep]. - Q4 Dry run and confirmation: (a) always a dry run first, `[y/N]` per project with Enter as no, `--yes` skips the questions, `--dry-run` stops after the preview [matrix.copy-confirm].
- Q5 Apply to all and a partial failure: (a) dry-run every target first and write nothing if any dry run fails; then write each target with `expect`, go on after a write failure, `partial: true`, exit 1 [matrix.copy-all].
- Q6 Write path: (a) only through slicer's atomic `relay-roles apply` replace (slicer s443 and s444, then ork S250); settled by the 2026-11-10 note.
- Q7 Where it appears and its name: (a) the CLI `ork roles matrix copy FROM (TO... | --all)` and the daemon method `matrix.copy`; a TUI action is a later item on S226 or S251 [matrix.copy-surface].
- Q8 Pass: (b) v1.2, with S250, and S261 depends on S250; settled by the 2026-11-10 note.
